content:
# Disagreement Log — 1 Kings Chapter 6
**Reviewed by:** SOPHIA | **Date:** 2026-03-11

---

## Summary
25 verse(s) flagged for significant translation divergence.

### Verse 1
**EMET (literal):** And-it-was in-the-four-hundred and-eightieth year after-the-going-out-of the-sons-of Israel from-the-land-of Egypt, in-the-fourth year, in-the-month-of Ziv — it is the-second month — of-the-reigning-of Solomon over Israel, and-he-built the-house for-YHWH.

**LOGOS (formal):** In the four hundred and eightieth year after the people of Israel came out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign over Israel, in the month of Ziv, which is the second month, he began to build the house of the LORD.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Four hundred and eighty years after the Israelites came out of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign — in the month of Ziv, the second month — Solomon began building the temple of the LORD.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 3
**EMET (literal):** And-the-porch before the-temple-of the-house — twenty cubits its-length, upon the-face-of the-width-of the-house; ten cubits its-depth upon the-face-of the-house.

**LOGOS (formal):** The vestibule in front of the nave of the house was twenty cubits long, equal to the width of the house, and ten cubits deep in front of the house.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The entrance hall in front of the main hall was thirty feet wide, matching the width of the temple, and extended fifteen feet out from the front.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 5
**EMET (literal):** And-he-built against the-wall-of the-house a-structure all-around — against-the-walls-of the-house all-around, for-the-temple and-for-the-inner-sanctuary — and-he-made side-chambers all-around.

**LOGOS (formal):** He also built a structure against the wall of the house, running around the walls of the house, both the nave and the inner sanctuary. And he made side chambers all around.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Against the outer walls of the temple he built a multi-story annex around both the main hall and the inner sanctuary, with side rooms on every level.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 6
**EMET (literal):** The-lowest story — five cubits its-width, and-the-middle — six cubits its-width, and-the-third — seven cubits its-width. For he-made offsets in-the-wall-of the-house all-around on-the-outside, so-as-not to-fasten in-the-walls-of the-house.

**LOGOS (formal):** The lowest story was five cubits wide, the middle was six cubits wide, and the third was seven cubits wide. For around the outside of the house he made offsets on the wall so that the supporting beams would not be inserted into the walls of the house.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The lowest floor of the annex was seven and a half feet wide, the middle floor nine feet, and the top floor ten and a half feet. He made ledges on the outside of the temple wall so the annex beams would not have to be set into the temple walls themselves.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 7
**EMET (literal):** And-the-house, in-its-being-built, of-whole stone from-the-quarry was-built; and-hammer and-axe — any tool-of iron — was-not heard in-the-house in-its-being-built.

**LOGOS (formal):** When the house was built, it was with stone prepared at the quarry, so that neither hammer nor axe nor any tool of iron was heard in the house while it was being built.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The temple was built using blocks of stone finished at the quarry. No hammer, chisel, or any iron tool was heard at the building site during construction.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 8
**EMET (literal):** The-entrance-of the-lowest side-chamber was in-the-right shoulder-of the-house, and-by-winding-stairs they-would-go-up to the-middle, and-from the-middle to the-third.

**LOGOS (formal):** The entrance to the lowest story was on the south side of the house, and one went up by winding stairs to the middle story, and from the middle story to the third.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The entrance to the ground floor was on the south side of the temple, with a spiral staircase leading to the middle level and from there to the top level.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 9
**EMET (literal):** And-he-built ʾet-the-house, and-finished-it. And-he-covered ʾet-the-house with-beams and-rows-of cedar.

**LOGOS (formal):** So he built the house and finished it, and he roofed the house with beams and planks of cedar.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** So Solomon built the temple and completed it, roofing it with cedar beams and planks.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 10
**EMET (literal):** And-he-built ʾet-the-structure against all the-house — five cubits its-height — and-it-held the-house with-timber-of cedar.

**LOGOS (formal):** He built the structure against the whole house, five cubits high, and it was joined to the house with timbers of cedar.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He built the side structure along the entire temple, each story seven and a half feet high, attached to the temple with cedar timbers.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 12
**EMET (literal):** "This house that you are-building — if you-walk in-my-statutes and-ʾet-my-judgments you-do, and-keep ʾet-all my-commandments to-walk in-them, then-I-will-establish ʾet-my-word with-you that I-spoke to David your-father.

**LOGOS (formal):** "Concerning this house that you are building — if you will walk in my statutes and obey my rules and keep all my commandments and walk in them, then I will establish my word with you, which I spoke to David your father.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** "As for this temple you are building — if you walk in my decrees, carry out my laws, and keep all my commands by living according to them, I will fulfill through you the promise I made to your father David.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 13
**EMET (literal):** And-I-will-dwell in-the-midst-of the-sons-of Israel, and-I-will-not forsake ʾet-my-people Israel."

**LOGOS (formal):** And I will dwell among the children of Israel and will not forsake my people Israel."

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** I will live among the Israelites and will not abandon my people Israel."

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 15
**EMET (literal):** And-he-built ʾet-the-walls-of the-house on-the-inside with-boards-of cedar — from the-floor-of the-house to the-walls-of the-ceiling he-overlaid with-wood on-the-inside — and-he-overlaid ʾet-the-floor-of the-house with-boards-of cypress.

**LOGOS (formal):** He lined the walls of the house on the inside with boards of cedar. From the floor of the house to the rafters of the ceiling, he covered them on the inside with wood, and he covered the floor of the house with boards of cypress.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He paneled the interior walls with cedar boards from floor to ceiling and covered the floor with cypress planks.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 16
**EMET (literal):** And-he-built ʾet-the-twenty cubits from-the-rear-of the-house with-boards-of cedar from the-floor to the-walls, and-he-built for-it on-the-inside the-inner-sanctuary, the-Holy-of-Holies.

**LOGOS (formal):** He built twenty cubits of the rear of the house with boards of cedar from floor to ceiling, and he built this within as an inner sanctuary, as the Most Holy Place.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He partitioned off the rear thirty feet of the temple with cedar boards from floor to ceiling, creating the inner sanctuary — the Most Holy Place.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 17
**EMET (literal):** And-forty cubits was the-house — it is the-temple — before-it.

**LOGOS (formal):** The house, that is, the nave in front of the inner sanctuary, was forty cubits long.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The main hall in front of the inner sanctuary was sixty feet long.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 18
**EMET (literal):** And-cedar on-the-house on-the-inside — carvings-of gourds and-open flowers — all was cedar; no stone was-seen.

**LOGOS (formal):** The cedar within the house was carved in the form of gourds and open flowers. All was cedar; no stone was seen.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The cedar inside the temple was carved with gourds and open flowers. Everything was cedar — no stone could be seen.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 19
**EMET (literal):** And-the-inner-sanctuary in-the-midst-of the-house on-the-inside he-prepared, to-set there ʾet-the-ark-of the-covenant-of YHWH.

**LOGOS (formal):** The inner sanctuary he prepared in the innermost part of the house, to set there the ark of the covenant of the LORD.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He prepared the inner sanctuary deep within the temple as the place for the ark of the LORD's covenant.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 21
**EMET (literal):** And-Solomon overlaid ʾet-the-house on-the-inside with-gold refined, and-he-drew chains-of gold before the-inner-sanctuary, and-he-overlaid-it with-gold.

**LOGOS (formal):** And Solomon overlaid the inside of the house with pure gold, and he drew chains of gold across the front of the inner sanctuary, and overlaid it with gold.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Solomon overlaid the interior of the temple with pure gold. He stretched gold chains across the front of the inner sanctuary, which was also overlaid with gold.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 22
**EMET (literal):** And-ʾet-all the-house he-overlaid with-gold until all the-house was-finished. And-all the-altar that was-by the-inner-sanctuary he-overlaid with-gold.

**LOGOS (formal):** And he overlaid the whole house with gold, until all the house was finished. Also the whole altar that belonged to the inner sanctuary he overlaid with gold.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He covered the entire interior of the temple with gold — every surface. He also overlaid with gold the altar that stood before the inner sanctuary.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 23
**EMET (literal):** And-he-made in-the-inner-sanctuary two cherubim of-olive wood — ten cubits their-height.

**LOGOS (formal):** In the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim of olivewood, each ten cubits high.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Inside the inner sanctuary he made two cherubim out of olive wood, each fifteen feet tall.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 24
**EMET (literal):** And-five cubits was-the-one wing-of the-cherub, and-five cubits the-second wing-of the-cherub — ten cubits from-the-tip-of his-wing to the-tip-of his-wing.

**LOGOS (formal):** Five cubits was the length of one wing of the cherub, and five cubits the length of the other wing of the cherub; it was ten cubits from the tip of one wing to the tip of the other.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Each wing of the first cherub was seven and a half feet long — fifteen feet from wingtip to wingtip.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 25
**EMET (literal):** And-ten cubits was the-second cherub — one measure and-one form for-the-two cherubim.

**LOGOS (formal):** The other cherub also measured ten cubits; both cherubim had the same measure and the same form.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** The second cherub also measured fifteen feet. Both cherubim were identical in size and shape.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 26
**EMET (literal):** The-height-of the-one cherub was ten cubits, and-so the-second cherub.

**LOGOS (formal):** The height of one cherub was ten cubits, and so was that of the other cherub.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** Each cherub stood fifteen feet tall.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 27
**EMET (literal):** And-he-set ʾet-the-cherubim in-the-midst-of the-inner house. And-they-spread ʾet-the-wings-of the-cherubim, and-the-wing-of the-one touched the-wall, and-the-wing-of the-second cherub touched the-second wall. And-their-wings toward-the-middle-of the-house were-touching wing to wing.

**LOGOS (formal):** He put the cherubim in the innermost part of the house. And the wings of the cherubim were spread out so that a wing of one touched the one wall, and a wing of the other cherub touched the other wall; their wings touched one another in the middle of the house.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He placed the cherubim inside the inner sanctuary. Their wings were spread so that one wing of the first cherub touched one wall and one wing of the second cherub touched the opposite wall, while their inner wings touched each other in the center of the room.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 33
**EMET (literal):** And-so he-made for-the-entrance-of the-temple doorposts-of olive wood — from a-fourth.

**LOGOS (formal):** So also he made for the entrance to the nave doorposts of olivewood, four-sided,

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** In the same way, for the entrance to the main hall he made doorposts of olive wood, four-sided.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 34
**EMET (literal):** And-two doors of-cypress wood — the-two leaves-of the-one door were-folding, and-the-two leaves-of the-second door were-folding.

**LOGOS (formal):** and two doors of cypress wood. The two leaves of the one door were folding, and the two leaves of the other door were folding.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** He also made two cypress doors, each with two hinged panels.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

### Verse 38
**EMET (literal):** And-in-the-eleventh year, in-the-month-of Bul — it is the-eighth month — the-house was-finished in-all its-matters and-in-all its-specifications. And-he-built-it in-seven years.

**LOGOS (formal):** And in the eleventh year, in the month of Bul, which is the eighth month, the house was finished in all its parts and according to all its specifications. He had been seven years in building it.

**PNEUMA (dynamic):** In the eleventh year, in the month of Bul — the eighth month — the temple was finished in every detail, exactly according to plan. It had taken seven years to build.

**SOPHIA resolution:** The divergence reflects translation philosophy differences rather than disagreement about the Hebrew text. LOGOS adopted as consensus baseline.

---

— SOPHIA
